cross_check.finding: For ALL 25753 unrated ACTIVE rows the most recent rating_changed event has an absent destination ('null'), or no rating_changed event exists at all. ZERO unrated ACTIVE rows have a most-recent ledger destination holding a real rating value. This is a FULL-POPULATION, measured check (not a sample) and it finds no internal evidence of a lost rating.
cross_check.predicate_used: trusted_event_ledger.new_value::text = 'null'  (new_value is jsonb; NEVER use IS NULL)
cross_check.query:
with ev as (
  select e.location_id as id, e.new_value::text as dest,
         row_number() over (partition by e.location_id order by e.observed_at desc nulls last, e.id desc) rn
    from trusted_event_ledger e
    join care_providers p on p.id = e.location_id
   where e.event_type = 'rating_changed' and p.status='ACTIVE'
     and (p.overall_rating IS NULL OR btrim(p.overall_rating) = ''))
select count(*) filter (where rn=1 and dest='null'), count(*) filter (where rn=1 and dest<>'null'),
       count(*) filter (where rn=1) from ev where rn=1
cross_check.question: does any independent internal record contradict the blank overall_rating?
cross_check.why: new_value/old_value are jsonb columns; a JSON null is the text 'null', not SQL NULL. Measured: new_value IS NULL -> 4 rows (all event_type='integration_connectivity'); new_value::text='null' -> 80306 rows.
